channel.title: The Indigenous Beacon
channel.description: Native-led journalism on Native American history, sovereignty, culture and contemporary life.

item.title: ICWA After Brackeen: What the Court Settled — and What It Left Open
item.description: The Indian Child Welfare Act survived the Supreme Court in 2023. Here is what the law actually requires of state agencies, what the Court decided, and which questions it never answered.

item.title: What the Federal Record Actually Shows About Indian Boarding Schools
item.description: 408 schools across 37 states. Over 500 documented child deaths at 19 schools. The Department of the Interior's own investigation put the numbers on the record — here is what it found and what it left unfinished.

item.title: Speaking the Language Home: Indigenous Language Revitalization
item.description: Across Indian Country, communities are reviving languages once forced into silence — through immersion schools, master-apprentice programs, and technology. A look at how, and why it matters.

item.title: The Three Sisters Return: Native Food Sovereignty
item.description: From seed rematriation to community gardens, Native communities are rebuilding food systems that nourish both people and land — reclaiming the right to define their own foodways.

item.title: 5 Stories Mainstream Media Missed This Month
item.description: A roundup of under-covered Native news that deserves your attention — from land returns to language revitalization.

item.title: The Cloud's New Frontier: Data Centers and Tribal Lands
item.description: As tech giants race to build data centers across the American West, Native American tribes are facing a complex new challenge — and an unexpected opportunity.

item.title: Land Back: What It Really Means
item.description: A policy explainer on the movement to return land to Indigenous stewardship — what it is, what it isn't, and where it's winning.

item.title: Meet the Makers: Sarah Ortegon
item.description: The Diné (Navajo) artist is carrying a centuries-old weaving tradition into the 21st century, one thread at a time.

item.title: Coded Invisibility: Native Americans in the Tech Industry and the Fight for Representation
item.description: Native people make up less than 1% of the tech workforce. A growing movement is trying to change that — and reshape the future of technology itself.

item.title: Teaching Native History Beyond November
item.description: How educators can integrate Indigenous perspectives into the classroom year-round — a practical guide for K-12 and beyond.

item.title: The Last Mile: How Native Nations Are Building Their Way Out of the Digital Divide
item.description: How Native nations are building their own broadband networks to bridge the digital divide, assert sovereignty, and connect their communities.

item.title: What Does It Mean to Be Native Today?
item.description: An exploration of the complexity, diversity, and resilience of contemporary Native American identity — beyond the stereotypes.

item.title: Why The Indigenous Beacon Exists
item.description: A Native-led platform for truth, told by those who live it. Read our launch story about why Indigenous representation in media matters.
